reason: As written the falsifier does not discriminate. (1) Metric ambiguity: 'trials to full rank' is undefined. If trials = candidate targets drawn from the decomposition oracle, a keep/discard policy cannot change it: the union graph of drawn weight-2 relations (columns = factor-base points) has the same connectivity/rank whatever is kept, so greedy == random exactly (a 0% result by construction, trivially satisfying prediction_if_false). If trials = relations kept, greedy keeps a spanning forest (~B-1 = 499) versus random ~(B/2)(ln B + gamma) ~ 1.6k, a >60% 'win' that is a definitional artefact (it shrinks the matrix, not the oracle cost) and trivially satisfies prediction_if_true. Neither outcome tests the claimed mechanism, which requires STEERING target choice toward uncovered columns; no steering model or covariate is specified, and the card's own risk line says steering is impossible. (2) No null/control arm is named; no oracle-granted upper-bound arm. (3) Statistics: coupon-collector-type completion time has relative sd ~ 1.28/(ln B + 0.58) ~ 0.19 at B=500; with 50 independent runs per arm the SE of a difference of means is ~3.8% unpaired, larger than the stated 3% null band, so a true-null result would land outside +-3% roughly 40% of the time; the 15% threshold is about 4 SE, fine, the 3% band is not. (4) Runnability: feasible (p~2^20, B=500, m=2 decomposition prob ~ B^2/(2r) ~ 0.12/target, ~500 membership lookups per target, ~1.6k relations needs ~13k targets ~ 6.5M set lookups: numpy/hash-set seconds, gp tens of seconds); well under 20 CPU-min if the relation pool is built once and arms are replayed over resampled orderings. (5) Scaling to n=131: toy says nothing beyond the constant. Best possible gain from coupon effects is bounded by 1 - O(1/ln B) (a log B factor, <=~6.2 at B=500, ~log of the 2^~43 base at 131 bits), a constant/log factor, not an exponent; B*D^2 << N certificate untouched; classification stays engineering. Structural quantity (rank, draws) is the right kind of metric (counted, not wall time); fix must pin down which count.
fix: Redesign as a three-arm paired experiment with the cost fixed as ORACLE CALLS (candidate targets tested for decomposition) to reach rank = (#cols - 1) over Z/ell for a toy prime-order ell (rank over F_ell; columns = +/-P_i classes; one extra dlog column). Build once with PARI/python: E over F_p, p~2^20 prime order r; factor base B=500 (x-coordinates, negation-quotient); for random aP+bQ test m=2 decomposition by hash-set lookup of R-P_i; store relation pool (>=20k targets, with their (a,b), x(R), decomposition columns). Arms replayed on the SAME pool via common random numbers: (A) random-accept-all [baseline]; (B) greedy-keep/rank-aware filtering of the same drawn stream [NULL CONTROL: must give identical draws-to-full-rank, asserted exactly; kept-count reported separately, labelled matrix-size not cost]; (C) ORACLE-STEERED upper bound: cheat with known dlogs/pool to draw next target whose decomposition hits an uncovered column (the best any policy could do; gain bounded by coupon theory ~1-2/ln B). Report C-vs-A as the maximal conceivable gain; if C-vs-A < 15% the idea is dead even with a free steering oracle. Then the decisive realism test: steerability = mutual information / chi-square between cheap target features (a,b mod small moduli, x(R) bits, low bits of x(R), residue of x(R) mod B) and the decomposition column index, versus a label-permutation control (>=1000 permutations); steering exists only if p<1e-3 after Bonferroni, expected null (generic group ~ random-oracle). Statistics: >=200 paired resamples (bootstrap orderings), report paired difference with 95% CI; pre-register prediction_if_false as CI of (B-A) containing 0 and C-A < 15%, prediction_if_true as steerability test significant AND C-A>=15%. Also run at p~2^16 and 2^22, B in {250,500,1000} to show gain scales as 1/ln B (constant/log factor), then state plainly no n=131 extrapolation beyond that factor. CPU <=10 min in python3+numpy (+gp for ellcard/point generation).
